requirement: Public, reproducible dataset access and license
why: The fifth dataset must be auditable before preprocessing or scoring.

requirement: User-item interaction rows with stable user_id and item_id
why: Every paper metric depends on user/item identity and held-out targets.

requirement: Chronological order or timestamps
needed_by_metric_analysis: leave-one-out split, history sensitivity, sequential models, profile generation
why: Histories must be truncated and targets held out consistently.

requirement: Item titles or names
needed_by_metric_analysis: LLM prompts, hallucination, profile generation, BM25
why: The paper forms histories and candidates from item titles.

requirement: Item metadata categories/tags/genres
why: Paper/code diversity and local extensions need feature coverage.

requirement: Train-only item popularity counts
needed_by_metric_analysis: ARP, APLT, PopREO, SelfInformation local adaptation, MostPop
why: Popularity metrics and MostPop primitive require frozen popularity source.

requirement: Unique-user item popularity counts
why: Paper formula uses |U| and |U_i|.

requirement: Ground-truth positive target per sampled user
why: Utility and hit-conditioned metrics require the held-out item.

requirement: Ranking candidate pools with one positive and 19 negatives
needed_by_metric_analysis: ranking utility, hallucination/candidate validity, ItemCoverage, OIC, CandDif
why: The paper ranking setting uses 20 candidates.

requirement: Reranking candidate pools from BPRMF, GRU4Rec, SASRec, and LightGCN top-K outputs
why: The paper reranking setting forms 20-item pools from four traditional models.

requirement: Candidate order and positive position metadata
why: Position perturbation cannot be evaluated without candidate positions.

requirement: History length bins with sufficient depth
why: Users must have histories deep enough for the selected bins.

requirement: Aligned MostPop recommendation/hit vector
why: Serendipity uses a MostPop primitive and must share cohort/candidates.

requirement: Popularity quintile groups with zero-denominator policy
why: PopREO divides items into five popularity groups and can fail with empty groups.

requirement: User activity groups based on median history length
why: DPD compares active and inactive users.

requirement: Catalog item universe with exposure denominator policy
why: Paper Gini and hallucination require item universe definitions.

requirement: Free-text/title-list LLM outputs or paper-equivalent parser outputs
why: Paper hallucination is based on string matching, not only JSON/index validity.

requirement: Profile-generation outputs and dependency manifest
why: Profile-only and profile-plus-history conditions depend on generated profiles.

requirement: Traditional model training-ready split and configs
why: Paper compares against six trained/traditional systems.

requirement: Raw output manifests, parser provenance, and invalid-output policy
needed_by_metric_analysis: LLM utility, hallucination, strict validity, duplicate rate
why: Local reproduction parity depends on explicit denominator and parser policies.

requirement: Candidate retrieval and aggregation intermediate artifacts
needed_by_metric_analysis: Candidate Recall, oracle ceiling, pipeline decomposition
why: Pipeline-aware extensions require upstream candidate-stage evidence.

requirement: Positive-injection intervention records
needed_by_metric_analysis: positive injection, conditional vs end-to-end utility
why: Future interventions must be auditable and separated from paper framework.

requirement: Token, latency, and cost logs
why: Useful for budget planning but not a paper metric.
